sources.note: Nothing; states the language is unwritten, unclassified within Benue-Congo, extinct in the 2000s; cites Ethnologue and Williamson (1989).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. 2020 edition (version of 11 September 2020). Cambridge: McDonald Institute for Archaeological Research (author-circulated PDF, 198 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing. Front matter sec. 4.1 (PDF p.10, p. v): 'Fali of Baissa: Spoken by a few individuals on the Falinga Plateau in southern Taraba State. A fragmentary wordlist was recorded by Robert Koops in the early 1970s, suggesting that the language is clearly Benue-Congo, but its further affiliation is uncertain.' Index (p.29): 'Fali of Baissa – nearly extinct'; no head entry, no phonological data; listed under 'Unclassified Benue-Congo languages: Fali (in Baissa area; virtually extinct)'.
